goal: Diplomacy and war: lead a nation, meet a neighbour, try alliance, rivalry and war from the Nations screen (O). This build adds an envoy: every diplomacy act that takes effect (gift/tribute, alliance, denunciation, war, peace) sends your envoy to that nation and blocks further acts toward that nation for 1,000 ticks (20 s of play, which pass only while the Nations screen is closed). Check that acts toward one nation now take game time, that the status line and the Nations screen row explain the wait, that a refused offer sends no envoy, and that each nation has its own envoy. Record the game tick of each act.

findings.title: Nations screen at ~1 fps treats every frame as a reopen: War/Denounce confirm never holds and rows re-sort under the pointer
findings.detail: At 1-2 fps the Nations screen disarms the two-click confirm between frames. Denounce on Northport showed 'Confirm' on the button, but two quick click pairs each left 'Click Denounce again to denounce Northport.' and nothing happened. One War pair did go through. The kept row order is also dropped, so rows re-sort while the screen is open. After War on Whitewood (tick 2644), Whitewood jumped to row 1 and Southernport's War button slid under the pointer. After Peace (tick 3728), Whitewood dropped back to row 2, and a click aimed at Southernport's Tribute hit Whitewood instead. Cause seen in the source (read-only): NationScreen.ReopenGapSeconds = 1.0, measured between frames with ImGui.GetTime, so any frame gap over 1 s clears shownOrder and disarms the ConfirmGate. Expected: a reopen is detected from the screen being closed, not from frame time, so confirms and row order survive slow frames.
findings.repro: pt start --profile beyond-nations --game-dir /root/bn-wt-playtest064 --seed 104 (on a loaded machine, fps 1); key n; wait until 2+ AI nations exist; key o; pt click on a War or Denounce button twice ~1 s apart; or act on row 1 and watch the rows re-order

findings.title: Status line says 'deal with them again in 20 seconds' and never counts down, contradicting the row
findings.detail: After a blocked act, the status line reads 'Your envoy to Southernport is still on the road: you can deal with them again in 20 seconds of play.' The text stays on the world HUD and on the Nations screen. 264 ticks later the row above it correctly said 'envoy back in 15 s', but the status line still said 20 seconds. Expected: the status line counts down, or is cleared once the countdown no longer matches.
findings.repro: lead a nation; key o; Tribute nation A; Tribute A again (blocked); Escape; pt wait 40; key o; compare the row's 'envoy back in N s' with the status line

findings.title: War/Denounce ask for confirmation even when the envoy is away and the act will be refused
findings.detail: With the envoy to Southernport away (row: 'envoy back in 20 s'), clicking War gives 'Click War again to declare war on Southernport'. Only the confirming click says 'Your envoy to Southernport is still on the road'. Denounce behaves the same. The buttons for a nation whose envoy is away also look exactly as enabled as normal ones. Expected: the buttons are dimmed, or the envoy message shows on the first click.
findings.repro: key o; Tribute Southernport; click War on Southernport twice quickly

findings.title: New nations appear mid-list between visits, so a remembered button position hits the wrong nation
findings.detail: Between two visits to the Nations screen, the new nation Whitewood was inserted as row 2, above Castleton. My War click meant for Castleton's row declared war on Whitewood (tick 2644). Sorting 'neighbours and enemies first' is reasonable, but nothing marks a new row as new. A 'new' tag or a highlight on new nations would help.
findings.repro: seed 104; key n; key o at ~tick 1500 (2 nations), close, reopen at ~tick 2600 (Whitewood is row 2)

findings.title: Three tributes at the envoy pace land at +29 because of relation decay, one short of the +30 an alliance needs
findings.detail: The header says tribute gives +10 and an alliance needs +30. Gifts to Southernport at ticks 1508, 2644 and 3728 (as fast as the envoy allows) gave +10, +20, then +29, because relations decay about 1 point per envoy round trip. An alliance therefore needs a 4th gift (100 coins) and a 5th envoy window, over 60 s of play. I could not reach an alliance within the time budget. Either make three gifts enough, or have the header say that relations fade.
findings.repro: key n; key o; Tribute nation A every time its envoy returns; read relations after the 3rd gift

findings.title: Game runs at 1-2 fps and 5-9 ticks/s, so each 20 s envoy wait takes ~3 minutes of real time
findings.detail: pt status showed fps 1-3 and tps 5.6-16.7 for the whole session, on a machine shared with other sessions. The envoy design ties every diplomacy act to 1,000 ticks, which made this goal slow to test.

verdict: The envoy works as designed. Accepted acts send a separate envoy to each nation, refused offers send none, and blocked acts take no coins. The Nations row counts down 'envoy back in N s', and the header explains the rule well. The major problem is the Nations screen at low frame rates: with frame gaps over 1 s the two-click confirm never holds and rows re-sort under the pointer, which sent one of my clicks to the wrong nation. The status line's frozen '20 seconds' and relation decay leaving three gifts at +29 also need a look.
